operations.title: The finite-group norm has a sharp characteristic dichotomy
operations.statement: For every nontrivial finite group G over a field k, x nu_G=epsilon(x)nu_G and nu_G^2=|G|nu_G. If char(k) does not divide |G|, nu_G/|G| is the central idempotent onto the trivial summand. If char(k) divides |G|, norm multiplication is square-zero with homology ker(epsilon)/(k nu_G) of dimension |G|-2 per regular fiber.
operations.scope: Regular group-algebra fibers only; no physical relative-chain transfer or physical-readout identification.

operations.title: S3 bad-characteristic hostile control
operations.procedure: Apply the coefficient-permutation identity to the regular module k[S3] in characteristics two and three. In both cases the kernel has dimension five and the norm image dimension one, leaving four homology dimensions. In characteristic five the normalized norm is instead an idempotent.
operations.expected_result: Four residual dimensions at characteristics two and three, and an idempotent normalized projector at characteristic five. Any contrary regular-module rank falsifies the claim.
